title: VPC microsegmentation playbook and evidence flow checklist
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a practical, ops-focused playbook for implementing microsegmentation inside Redwood Private deployments. It assumes customers require strong network boundaries, mTLS between service tiers, RBAC v2 audit hooks, and automated evidence collection to feed a SIEM. The goal is a repeatable checklist operators can follow and an evidence pipeline that produces tamper-evident artifacts for audits.

High-level approach (intent first):
1) Define service trust domains (control-plane, model-serving, logging, customer-vms).
2) Apply label-driven microsegmentation at L3/L4 using provider Security Groups / Firewall Policies and service-aware L7 controls where available.
3) Enforce mutual TLS for east-west connections between trust domains with short-lived certs and key rotation automation.
4) Capture RBAC v2 role and binding snapshots and correlate with network decisions in audit logs.
5) Automate evidence extraction and push normalized records into SIEM (CEF/Elastic Common Schema).

Network pattern summary (recommended):
- Minimal cross-domain access: only explicit ports/protocols allowed per service contract.
- Service gateway for north-south from customer networks; deny direct host-to-host unless signed off.
- Host-bound interfaces: VMs/instances only open loopback ports for sidecars; sidecars handle mTLS and auditing.
- Labeled security groups: use tags like svc:ingress, svc:inference, tier:worker, env:prod to drive firewall rules.

Example firewall rule intent (human-readable):
- allow: inference-worker -> model-pool tcp/443 mTLS only (src-tag: svc:inference, dst-tag: svc:model-pool)
- allow: model-pool -> kv-store tcp/6379 tls-required (src-tag: svc:model-pool, dst-tag: svc:kv)
- deny: customer-vms -> control-plane * (default deny, require explicit exception)
- allow: logging -> siem-ingest tcp/9200 only from logging subnet

Cloud-native rule example (pseudo-Cloud):
- FirewallPolicy: inference-to-models
  - match: srcTags=[svc:inference] dstTags=[svc:model-pool] protocols=[TCP:443] action=ALLOW requireMTLS=true
  - audit: attach policy-id and terraform-address to rule metadata for evidence

mTLS architecture and rotation (ops notes):
- Use a short-lived intermediate CA (validity 24 hours), signed by customer-managed root (KMS/HSM).
- Certificate issuance flow: workload requests cert via CSR to local agent -> agent authenticates via instance identity -> CA issues cert -> agent writes to ephemeral keystore path and signals sidecar.
- Sidecar pattern: envoy (or lightweight proxy) enforces mTLS and exposes plain HTTP only to local loopback for app.
- Rotation: staggered 6-hour overlap windows, automated by agent; verify TLS chains and push rotation event to audit pipeline.

mTLS handshake ASCII flow (simplified):
- Client sidecar -> TLS ClientHello -> Server sidecar -> ServerHello, CertChain -> Client validates chain against intermediate CA -> Client sends CertificateVerify -> mutually authenticated channel established

RBAC v2 mapping (operators):
- Roles (examples): network-auditor, network-approver, deployment-operator, evidence-admin
- RoleBindings: map to idp groups (okta/redwood-sso) and service principals (infra CI accounts)
- Constraint: network-approver is the only role allowed to create firewall policy exceptions in prod. All changes must have linked change request id.

Audit log schema (normalized text snippet):
- Fields we emit for each network-affecting event:
  - event_id: UUID
  - timestamp: ISO8601
  - actor: principal id (user/service)
  - actor_role_snapshot: comma-separated roles at time of change
  - action: firewall.create|firewall.update|cert.rotate|policy.attach
  - target: terraform_address | resource_id
  - change_delta: brief text summary
  - evidence_refs: list of artifact ids (hashes)
  - sha256_manifest: base64-sha256 of the archived evidence bundle

Sample audit log line (CEF-ish single-line, normalized):
<165>1 2024-11-02T14:12:03Z redwood-inference network-ops 1234 - event_id=3f2a... actor=alice@redwood.com action=firewall.update target=terraform:google_compute_firewall.inference-allow change_delta="added rule allow mTLS 443" evidence_refs=[evidence-20241102-42] sha256_manifest=Ab3f...

Evidence automation (playbook):
- On change commit/PR merge to infra repo: run terraform plan -> save plan.json and plan.sha256 -> run terraform apply -> capture apply.log and state-diff; collect associated PR id and approver.
- Post-apply: run evidence-collector agent that performs:
  1) resource snapshot (describe/list API)
  2) fetch live firewall rules and compare to plan
  3) capture cert chain from running sidecars (cert.pem and chain), store fingerprint
  4) capture control-plane RBAC bindings (roles, rolebindings) via API
  5) package artifacts as tar.gz, compute sha256, sign with infra key (kms-sign)
  6) upload to evidence-bucket with object metadata: {event_id, actor, pr_id, sha256}
  7) emit audit log pointing to evidence object and manifest hash

SIEM export mapping (recommended fields):
- ecs.message = human-friendly summary
- ecs.event.id = event_id
- ecs.actor.id = actor
- ecs.network.transport = tcp/udp
- ecs.network.direction = outbound/inbound
- ecs.file.hash.sha256 = sha256_manifest
- ecs.labels = tags used for rule

Sample normalized SIEM JSON (as a single-line payload to ingest pipeline):
{
  "event": {"id":"3f2a...","type":"network.change","created":"2024-11-02T14:12:03Z"},
  "user": {"id":"alice@redwood.com"},
  "network": {"direction":"outbound","transport":"tcp","port":443},
  "files": {"sha256":"Ab3f..."},
  "evidence_refs": ["evidence-20241102-42"]
}

Checklist (operational run):
- [ ] Confirm trust domains and label taxonomy documented and approved by security.
- [ ] Ensure default-deny firewall baseline exists for prod vpc.
- [ ] Implement sidecar mTLS and validate cert chains in staging.
- [ ] Configure rotation agent and run dry-run rotate in staging.
- [ ] Add terraform plan capture and enable evidence-collector job on apply.
- [ ] Configure SIEM ingestion mapping and validate field parity with audit logs.
- [ ] Snapshot RBAC v2 role-bindings and store with evidence bundle.
- [ ] Smoke test service-to-service flows with packet capture limited to test window and upload pcap to evidence bucket.

Troubleshooting notes (common failures):
- TLS validation fails after rotation: check CA chain order and time skew between hosts.
- Firewall rule not applied: confirm terraform state matches cloud provider; run provider API describe then reapply.
- Evidence manifest mismatch: compare plan.sha256 to uploaded tar.gz sha256 and validate KMS signature.

Operational hints and small scripts:
- Quick evidence pull (bash):
  curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://evidence.internal/api/v1/objects?event_id=3f2a" -o evidence-3f2a.tar.gz
  sha256sum evidence-3f2a.tar.gz
- Verify signed manifest (kms):
  kms-verify --key infra-audit-key --signature manifest.sig --payload manifest.json

Acceptance criteria for audits:
- Each prod network change must have: PR id, approver, plan.json, apply.log, resource-snapshot.json, cert-fingerprints, RBAC snapshot, tar.gz with sha256 and KMS signature. Audit extractor should be able to fetch by event_id and validate sha256.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Decide canonical ECS field mapping for actor_role_snapshot (single field vs nested).
- Add CI gate to prevent firewall changes without evidence artifacts attached.
- Standardize pcap retention policy and redaction for customer payloads.

References and links:
- Confluence: Network Standards (internal) -> CONFLUENCE-1234
- Infra repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infrastructure (PR template includes audit fields)
- SRE-Runbook: incident procedures for mTLS outages -> CONFLUENCE-5678

Notes to self: follow up with security on whether evidence-bucket needs HSM-backed encryption and with compliance on how long to keep plan.json for SOC2.
